title: Binance hack: developing story
summary: The largest crypto theft on record: attackers drained Binance hot wallets on ten blockchains on Oct 29; about US$3 billion has been frozen, deposits work again and Binance expects withdrawals to start resuming within 48 hours, and it says it will cover the losses.

facts.label: Stolen
facts.note: Binance's own estimate of the impact (Reuters); TRM Labs US$6.36B at the time taken; Chainalysis at least US$5.9B

facts.label: Frozen so far
facts.note: Binance said verified frozen assets reached US$3B (00:52 UTC Oct 30); Tether over US$1.567B USDT, Circle over US$800M USDC, First Digital froze the FDUSD involved

facts.label: Still with the attacker
facts.note: beyond the reach of issuers, per TRM Labs (as of 00:30 UTC Oct 30). These figures come from different sources and times (Binance for the total and the frozen amount, TRM Labs for this one), so stolen, frozen and still with the attacker need not add up

facts.label: Recovered
facts.note: frozen funds have not been reported as returned

facts.label: When
facts.note: most of it within about 20 minutes

facts.label: Who
facts.note: not confirmed by Binance or any government yet

facts.label: Binance
facts.value: deposits working normally; withdrawals still paused, expected to start resuming within 48 hours; says it will cover all losses
facts.note: Co-founder Yi He said on Oct 30 that deposits operate normally and withdrawals should start resuming within 48 hours while the withdrawal system and address controls are rebuilt (The Defiant; Coinpedia). Preliminary finding: a compromised engineer's laptop let an attacker submit unauthorized withdrawals; no evidence of a private-key leak. Binance.US not affected.
